The one-shot index was built on a **virtual machine with 1792 GB of DDR3 RAM** and dual Xeon E7-8890v3 processors (32 vCPUs) (p. 7).

**Machine name:** The name is garbled in this text conversion. It appears as "▼✻✹✲✸✷♠a115". Elsewhere the same glyph substitution maps ▼→M, ✻→6, ✹→4, ✲→-, ✸→3, ✷→2, ♠→m and a115→s. By that mapping the name is probably **M64-32ms**. This is my reconstruction, so check the PDF before quoting it (p. 7).

**How it was used (p. 8):** Building the single billion-point index (L = 125, R = 128, α = 2) on this machine took about 2 days. Peak memory use was about 1100 GB, and the resulting index had an average degree of 113.9.

**Contrast:** The merged index and the search experiments used the z840 workstation, which has 64 GB of RAM (pp. 7–8).
